title: Shared fake DOM models <select>.value; move the suites stopped on it
description:
## Goal

The shared fake DOM (`tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`) models `<select>.value` the way a browser does, so the client suites that stopped on it can move onto the shared fake. Each suite is then deleted from the census list.

## Context

The fake-DOM move (LIN-4252, LIN-4255) took the census of hand-written client-test fakes from 56 files to 25. Of the files left, 9 stopped on an API the fake doesn't model. Several of those stops are `<select>.value`: `lin-3833-run-control`, `prompt-section-task-mode` and `settings-take`, per the census comments. The fake throws on a write and returns `undefined` on a read (`fake-dom.js` around lines 80–85).

Two Surveys of LIN-4292 (at `af55cb737`) both name this as the real unblocker. It is also why the run-quota and runner-link reader stubs (`readDispatchExecControls`, which reads `select.value` at `common.js` around line 1765) stay stubs.

## This step

* **Model** `<select>.value` **and** `selectedIndex` **as a browser does,** with cases in `fake-dom.test.js`:
  * reading gives the selected option's value, or the first option's when none is marked selected;
  * writing selects the matching option, or none if nothing matches.
  * Also `<option>.selected`, and whatever reading an option's `value` needs (its text when there is no `value` attribute).
* **Move each suite whose census stop is** `<select>.value`**,** with test names and counts unchanged. Delete each one's census entry.
* **Replace the reader stubs in run-quota and runner-link** with the real reader where the fake can now answer.
* **A suite that still stops** on something else stays listed, with that API named as the new reason.

**Not this ticket:**

* the 16 single-element stubs (LIN-4254, which runs after this);
* the `querySelector` guards (LIN-4292);
* the witness default (its own ticket, after LIN-4254).

## Done when

* `fake-dom.test.js` pins the select model.
* Every `<select>.value` stop has either moved, or stays listed with a different, named reason.
* The census count falls by the number moved.
* The full unit suite passes.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 19:16–19:17, at `af55cb737`) corrected it. Here is the person's scope call, in order:

1. **Pins first, checked against a real browser.** The description's two rules conflict:
   * "the first option when none is marked" is the reset rule on parse or insert;
   * a write that matches nothing gives `selectedIndex -1` and `value ''`.

   Model selectedness per option, with a **dirty flag like** `checked` (`fake-dom.js` around line 332). Pin these in `fake-dom.test.js`:
   * the markup default, and the first option when none is marked;
   * the last `selected` wins;
   * the reset skips `disabled` options;
   * a no-match write gives `-1`/`''`;
   * `option.value` falls back to its collapsed text;
   * a dirty `option.selected`, and `innerHTML` resetting it.

   **Before pinning each expectation, check it once in Chromium** (Playwright is in the repo; a scratch script, with its output pasted in the PR), so the fake pins the right browser.
2. **Model** `select.options` **along with** `value` **and** `selectedIndex`**.** Production uses them together (`common.js` around 1796–1797 and 1839, `roadmap.js:439`, `settings-models.js:28`). Without `options`, `options[selectedIndex]` throws a bare TypeError rather than a `FakeDomError` that names the API. In the fake's "Deliberately not modelled" list, the bare `select` means the `select()` method, so write it as `select()`.
3. **Probe the three listed stops, cheapest first, and credit each one honestly.**
   * `prompt-section-task-mode` never reads a select (it stubs `readDispatchExecControls`), so its census reason is wrong. Move it if it can move. If it stops on something else (open-0 expects `document.createElement('a').click()`), list it with that reason.
   * `lin-3136-settings-take-predicate` really reads `scopeSelect.value`.
   * `lin-3833-run-control` goes **last, in its own commit, with a stop rule.** Its `c.fire('change', {dataset, value})` calls must set a real `<select>`, whose values are real options from `decision-panel.js`, and call that node's listeners. If that needs more than real controls plus `listenersOf`, stop and list it with the reason.
   * The PR says how many moved for the select model and how many were relabelled. Don't count a mislabelled move as the model's.
4. **The reader stubs in run-quota and runner-link become the real** `readDispatchExecControls`**, wrapped in a recording spy.** That keeps the `calls.readers.at(-1) === panel` asserts. The voices disagree on what the real reader returns for an untouched harness select: `''` (so `{null, null}`), or a pre-selected `'claude-code'` (`common.js` around 1713–1715). **Check it with a test and pin what is true.** Add one case that sets a value and asserts `dispatchPrompt`'s arguments.
5. **In the same PR:**
   * delete the dead `browserMarkup` in `real-dispatch-disclosure.js` (the fake's `NAMED` set already decodes those entities; this comes off LIN-4297's list);
   * fix the stale line references in the census comments and the fake's header (`prompt-section.js:1565` is now 1602, `:2714` is now 2741; `p0.test.js:897` cites `common.js:1263`, now 1758).

**Not this ticket:** naming symbols rather than line numbers in census comments, and stop reasons as asserted data (LIN-4297); `p0`'s re-implemented reader contract (LIN-4254); the 16 stubs (LIN-4254).

## At merge

* The Chromium check output is in the PR.
* `fake-dom.test.js` pins dirty selectedness and `options`.
* The moved suites keep their names and counts.
* Each remaining select-listed file has a reason that is true now.
* The census count, and the moved-versus-relabelled split, are stated.
* The full unit suite passes.

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out.* The plan was implemented as approved in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2317](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2317>) (squash-merged as `b581ac92`). Deviations: the reader witnesses went into new files `lin-4296-dispatch-reader` and `lin-4296-scope-pick` so the moved suites keep their names and counts; and three review fixes were made at close-out (select reset only on option/optgroup insert or remove, an inserted selected option wins, and the `rebuildDispatchModelOptions` witness), commit `86a1141b`. Census 25 → 22: 2 moved for the select model (`lin-3136-settings-take-predicate`, `lin-3833-run-control`), 1 moved for another reason (`prompt-section-task-mode`), 0 relabelled. The full plan text, the Decisions and the witness list are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4296 @ af55cb737

Read at `af55cb737` (LinearViewer). The census (`fake-dom-census.test.js:52-78`) lists 25 files; 9 have a stop reason, and 3 of those are `select`.

**Why it will be hard**

1. **The two rules in "This step" conflict.** "The first option's when none is marked selected" is the reset that runs on parse or insert. A write that matches nothing gives `selectedIndex -1` and `value ''`, not the first option. So each option needs dirty selectedness, the way `checked` works at `fake-dom.js:332`. Two more browser rules: the last `selected` wins, and the reset skips `disabled` options. If `value` is computed from the markup, `fake-dom.test.js` will pin the wrong browser.

2. **Probably only one of the three suites is really stopped on `select`.**
   - `prompt-section-task-mode` stubs `readDispatchExecControls` (line 61) and never reads a select. Its download tests (206, 257) reach `document.createElement('a').click()` (`prompt-section.js:160-164`), and the shared fake has no `click()`. My forecast is that it re-stops there.
   - `lin-3136-settings-take` is mostly pure `buildKeyList` tests; only its `proxy.js` part touches the scope select.
   - `lin-3833-run-control` (46 tests) is the real one, and it is heavy. `c.fire('change', {dataset:{testid:'run-harness'}, value:'opencode'})` fires synthetic targets. On the shared fake, each fire has to set the real `<select>` and call `listenersOf('change')` with the real node, because `dispatchEvent` is inert. Each value must also be a real option in `decision-panel.js:202-281`, or a faithful write reads `''`.

3. **The real reader pins nothing on its own.** The swipe disclosure renders with `harnessDefault: ''` (`prompt-section.js:796`), so the harness select reads its first option, `''`. The real reader then returns `{null, null}`, the same as the stub. Removing the stub also loses `calls.readers`, which backs "the press hands the reader the drawn disclosure panel" (run-quota:271, runner-link:217). Wrap the real reader in a spy, and add a check that sets a value and asserts `dispatchPrompt`'s args.

4. **The nearby code needs more than `value`.** `rebuildDispatchModelOptions` and `updateDispatchModelHint` (`common.js:1790-1840`) use `select.options`, `option.outerHTML` and `option.dataset`. They run once the model-catalog fetch resolves; run-quota avoids that only because its `fetch` returns `ok:false`. Either model `.options` now or name it.

5. **The census line numbers are stale.** The write is at `prompt-section.js:1602`, not 1565, and the reader is at `common.js:1757-1773`.

**What I would do first**

Write the browser-checked `fake-dom.test.js` cases first:
- markup default, and the first option when none is marked;
- disabled options skipped, last `selected` wins;
- a no-match write giving `-1`/`''`;
- `option.value` falling back to collapsed text;
- a dirty `option.selected`, and `innerHTML` resetting it.

Then probe `task-mode`, which is cheap; if it stops on `click()`, re-label it. Do `lin-3833` last, in its own commit.

Expect 1–2 suites to move and 1–2 to be re-labelled. Say so up front, so "the census falls by the number moved" isn't read as 3.

## Survey global: LIN-4296 @ af55cb737

**Where it lands.** `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, its pins in `fake-dom.test.js`, the census list `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` (25 entries), and three suites. The area is improving: eight close-outs in a row each moved suites and recorded why the rest stopped. The form-state code (`value`, `checked`, `isValueControl` at :513) is small, and a select model fits it: an option is selected per its `selected` attribute until something writes to it, the way `checked` already works. Keep it small. Nothing in `lib/` or `public/` renders `<optgroup>` or a disabled `<option>`, and every emitted `<option>` is closed.

**What the obvious way does.**
- **The three stops differ.** `lin-3136-settings-take-predicate` really reads `scopeSelect.value` (`proxy.js:51`). Moving it is a gain: a pick that isn't an option in `render-proxy.js:51-55` will now read `''`, as in a browser. `lin-3833-run-control` also fires `change` with plain-object targets (`c.fire(…, {dataset, value})`), so its move includes rewriting how it fires events onto real controls. `prompt-section-task-mode` stubs `readDispatchExecControls: () => ({})` and draws a bare `<div>`, so it never reads a select. It could already have moved the way `prompt-section-p0` did, keeping the stub. Its census reason is wrong. Move it, but don't credit the select model for it.
- **Stale line references.** The census and the fake's header cite `prompt-section.js:1565` and `:2714-2715`. At BASE those lines are `:1602` and `:2741`. `p0.test.js:897` cites `common.js:1263`, which is now `:1758`.
- **Inventories nothing enforces.** The fake's header has a "files that use this fake today" list and a `select` stop paragraph. Both are edited by hand, and nothing fails when they drift. The bare `select` in "Deliberately not modelled" means the `select()` method. Once `<select>` is modelled, write it as `select()`. The stub comments in run-quota and runner-link need rewording too.
- **The real reader returns something different.** An untouched harness select pre-selects `claude-code` (`common.js:1713-1715`), so the real reader returns `harness: 'claude-code'` where the stub returned `null`. No assertion checks it, so the suites stay green and that path goes unpinned. Both suites also assert `calls.readers.at(-1) === panel` (run-quota :271, runner-link :217). Keep those by wrapping the real reader in a recording spy rather than dropping them.

**Better, at this ticket's cost.**
- Model `select.options` along with `selectedIndex`. Production uses them together (`common.js:1796-1797, 1839`, `roadmap.js:439`, `settings-models.js:28`). Without `options`, `options[selectedIndex]` throws a bare TypeError instead of a `FakeDomError` naming the API.
- Delete `browserMarkup` in `real-dispatch-disclosure.js`. It decodes `—`/`…` "which the fake does not decode", but the fake's `NAMED` set now does (:92). It's a second copy.
- Fix the stale line references in the same PR.

**Better still, not this ticket's.** `p0.test.js:896-900` re-implements the reader's contract "without a `<select>`". After this lands it can use the real reader, which fits LIN-4254's stub sweep. The census's stop comments pin line numbers, which drift (see above). Naming a symbol would last longer, but changing that is the census's own redesign.

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2317 (branch feat/lin-4296-select-value-fake-dom, head 74f684f1)

**Done.** The shared fake DOM models `<select>` and `<option>` as Chromium does (per-option selectedness with a dirty flag; the reset runs on every child-list change). Chromium probes for each pinned expectation are in the PR.

**Census:** 25 → 22 files. Moved for the select model: 2 (`lin-3136-settings-take-predicate`, `lin-3833-run-control`). Moved for another reason: 1 (`prompt-section-task-mode`, whose stop was wrong). Relabelled: 0.

**Evidence:** `npm run test:unit` 23,807 pass / 0 fail. Hermetic keyed and proxy arms (with mongod, +400d clock shift) 23,880 pass / 0 fail / 0 cancelled, zero non-loopback sockets. Secret scan pass. CI on the PR: Unit tests, all 4 E2E shards, Secret scan and CI success are all green.

Not merged (merge is the orchestrator's or a human's).

## Review — LIN-4296

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2317, reviewed at head `74f684f1a7cea64c458c046fcbbbfc45b33b3de6` (base `af55cb737`, which is still the tip of main, so nothing changed on the touched files after the ticket was written).

CI: green on 74f684f1. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed.

### Scope against the plan
All seven planned commits landed, in order. These deviations have reasons, and I accept them:
- The reader witnesses went into a new file, `lin-4296-dispatch-reader` (2 cases), and the scope-pick case went into `lin-4296-scope-pick` (1 case). The plan put them inside the existing suites; moving them keeps those suites' names and counts unchanged.
- The catalog-apply test was skipped as conditional. I don't accept that one. See ledger item 3.

I re-ran the moved and rewired suites on base and on head with TAP output. Test names and counts are identical: lin-3833 46, lin-3136 13, task-mode 23, run-quota 14, runner-link 13. The census goes from 25 to 22: 2 moved for the select model, 1 moved for another reason (task-mode), 0 relabelled. That split is honest. task-mode keeps its `readDispatchExecControls: () => ({})` stub and records the anchor click with a suite-local `createElement` shim. The fake has no `click()`, and `select()` is still listed as not modelled.

**Regression check:** the only earlier fix this PR touches is LIN-4279's `replaceChild`. The old comment there said "inserted first, so a refused insert leaves `old` in place". The PR now removes before inserting, but the self- or ancestor-insert refusal is checked before anything changes, so that guarantee still holds. The `replaceChild` pins at `fake-dom.test.js:647-680` pass.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `resetAround` removed from `_insert` | fake-dom: 17 fail |
| `resetAround` removed from `_detach` | 10 fail |
| select read falls back to the first option (the "lazy shortcut") | 4 fail |
| `option.selected` setter no longer marks the option dirty | 1 fail |
| optgroup children dropped from `options` | 1 fail |
| reader stub restored in `lin-4296-dispatch-reader` | the chosen-value case fails |
| `lin-3833` `fire` never writes the value | 12 fail |
| select `value` setter made a no-op | lin-3833, lin-3136 and dispatch-reader: 11 fail |
| `lin-3833` read-back assert deleted | still green, as expected: every pick is a real option. The assert is a guard, not a witness. |

The load-bearing tests assert the right things.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "the select reset runs exactly when a browser runs it". The PR's 18-API matrix covers the tree-change APIs, but only for **unselected option** insertions and removals. I probed two siblings in Chromium (Playwright 1.57, `chromium-1228`) and against the fake at head. Both diverge. Both are inside the ticket's bounded class (plan Decision 2: "after each one, an option inserted into or removed from a select leaves the select in the state the browser gives"). No production code reaches either today: `observation.js:2587` and `swim.js:713` append unselected options, and `ship.js:1154`'s `remove(1)` already throws on the fake. But the fake's header claims they hold.

```
setup <select><option>a</option><option>b</option> </select>, then value='zz' (no match)
                                      chromium   fake@74f684f1
append(' ') (text node)               |-1        a|0
append a comment                      |-1        a|0
remove the trailing text node         |-1        a|0

setup [a, b(selected)]
insertBefore(n[selected attr], a)     n|0        b|2
insertBefore(n with .selected=true,a) n|0        b|2
```

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **inside** (bounded class: the select reset on child-list changes, plan Decision 2). The reset runs on *any* child-list change, but Chromium runs it only when an option or optgroup is inserted or removed. So a no-match write (`-1`/`''`) is undone by inserting or removing a text node or comment. That contradicts the fake's own header ("stays so until an option is inserted or removed"). **Settle before the merge (close-out fixes it):** in `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, `_insert` should call `resetAround(this)` only when `isOptionEl(node) || isOptgroupEl(node)`, and `_detach` should call `resetAround(parent)` only when `isOptionEl(this) || isOptgroupEl(this)`. Add a pin in `fake-dom.test.js`: `<option>a</option><option>b</option> ` inside a select, `value='zz'`, then `append(' ')`, then `append` a comment via `insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend','<!--c-->')`, then remove the trailing text node. After each step it should still read `''|-1` (Chromium, above). Distinguishing condition: before the fix the fake reads `a|0`.
2. **inside** (same class). Inserting an option that is already selected (by attribute or by `.selected=true`) does not take the selection. The fake applies "last in tree order wins", but Chromium makes the inserted selected option the selected one. **Settle before the merge (close-out fixes it):** add `onOptionsInserted(parent, node)` in `fake-dom.js`, called from `_insert` before the reset when the node is an option or optgroup. It finds the owner select (`parent`, or `parent.parentNode` when `parent` is an optgroup). If that select is single, it takes the last option in `[node]` (or in the optgroup's option children) whose `selectedOf` is true, and sets `_optSel = false` on every other option of the select. Add a pin: start with `[a, b(selected)]` and `insertBefore` an option `n` carrying a `selected` attribute before `a`. It should read `n|0` (Chromium). Repeat with `n.selected = true` instead of the attribute. Distinguishing condition: before the fix the fake reads `b|2`. **I trial-applied both fixes 1 and 2 at 74f684f1.** fake-dom, the lin-4296 suites, lin-3833, lin-3136, run-quota and runner-link stayed green (231 pass, 0 fail), and every probe above then matched Chromium. I reverted the trial afterwards. Close-out must re-run the full `npm run test:unit` on the fixed commit.
3. **inside** (plan step 3: the claim that `options` is modelled well enough for production, which the Surveys called necessary). No in-repo test runs `rebuildDispatchModelOptions` and `updateDispatchModelHint` (`common.js:1790-1840`: `options[0]`, `options[length-1].outerHTML`, `innerHTML` rebuild, `value` restore, `options[selectedIndex].dataset`) on the fake. The PR skipped the test because no catalog fetch resolves in the reader suites, but the plan meant it as the end-to-end witness either way. I ran a scratch test: build `renderDispatchExecControls('p', { harnessDefault: '' })` into a `loadWorld` document with `DISCLOSURE_SCRIPTS`, set `model.value` to a real option, then call `world.run('rebuildDispatchModelOptions')(model, 'opencode')`. It passes, and the value survives (`idx 1`). So this is a missing witness, not a model gap. **Settle before the merge:** close-out adds that case to `tests/unit/lin-4296-dispatch-reader.test.js`, asserting the prior model value is kept, `options[0].value === ''`, the last option is the `other…` sentinel, and the hint reads `''` or `'free'` without throwing.
4. **outside.** LIN-4297's list may still name `browserMarkup`, which this PR deleted. Close-out checks LIN-4297 and, if it is there, comments to drop it. This is not a merge condition.
5. **outside, not run.** Only Chromium was used as the reference, as the ticket specified. Firefox and WebKit behaviour on the reset and insertion edges was not checked. It is not needed for this deliverable, and the fake's header already names Chromium.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The model, the moves, the reader spies and the census are sound, and the mutation checks show the tests have teeth. Close-out still has to make three fixes before merge: the two reset divergences (items 1–2) and the missing rebuild witness (item 3). Each is named exactly above. Then it re-runs the full unit suite and CI on the new head.

## Close-out — LIN-4296

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2317, squash-merged as `b581ac92`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 86a1141b` (the commit CI passed on). Review verdict was Approve conditional on the ledger; no fresh go-ahead was needed. Test-only change (`tests/unit/**`, nothing in `lib/` or `public/`), so there is no deploy and no post-deploy step.

**Re-ground:** main moved from `af55cb73` to `8f97e18e` while the PR was open. Both new commits are docs/evidence files only; none touch the PR's files.

### Changes I made after approval (commit `86a1141b`)
- **Ledger 1** (review: reset runs on any child-list change): `_insert` and `_detach` in `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js` now run the select reset only when an option or optgroup is inserted or removed. Pin in `fake-dom.test.js`: `-1`/`''` survives appending a text node, a comment, and removing the trailing text node.
- **Ledger 2** (review: inserted selected option loses to the old one): new `onOptionsInserted` in the fake. An inserted option that is selected, by attribute or by `.selected = true`, takes the selection before the reset. Two pins: `[a, b(selected)]` with `n` inserted before `a` reads `n|0`, for both forms. Updated the two stale comments ("every child-list change") in the fake's header and reset helpers that this change made false.
- **Ledger 3** (review: no witness for the rebuild path): new case in `tests/unit/lin-4296-dispatch-reader.test.js` runs the real `rebuildDispatchModelOptions` / `updateDispatchModelHint` on a real disclosure. It asserts the prior model is kept, `options[0].value === ''`, the last option is `other…`, curated options sit between, and the hint reads `''` or `'free'` without throwing.

### Ledger
1. inside, **done**: the three new pins fail on the old fake (stashed it and re-ran: 3 fail) and pass on the fix.
2. inside, **done**: same check, same result.
3. inside, **done**: the witness runs the exact precondition the review named (a real model picked, then rebuilt for `opencode`) and passes.
4. outside, **done**: commented on LIN-4297 to drop the `browserMarkup` bullet, since this PR deleted it. No new ticket (LIN-4297 already carries the item).
5. outside, **filed**: LIN-4305 (Firefox/WebKit probe of the select reset edges), priority Low with the reasoning on the ticket, related to this ticket. The type label (`Improvement`) could not be set: the proxy has no label-write surface. The ticket says so.

### Not done / found along the way
- `lastChild` is not modelled on the shared fake (my first draft of a test hit it). Already covered by LIN-4291; no new ticket.

### CI
CI exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Run 42101516844 on `86a1141b`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all pass. Local `npm run test:unit` before the push: 23,811 pass, 0 fail (23,807 + 4 new tests). I did not re-run the hermetic keyed/proxy arms myself; CI runs the keyed one in place of `test:unit`.

### Census
25 → 22 files. Moved for the select model: 2 (`lin-3136-settings-take-predicate`, `lin-3833-run-control`). Moved for another reason: 1 (`prompt-section-task-mode`). Relabelled: 0.

Description pruned: the discharged Implementation Plan body is replaced by a stub (heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no` kept word for word). The pre-prune snapshot was verified in the task snapshots before the edit.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** The select model itself was small. The difficulty was fidelity. Twice, my reading of the spec disagreed with Chromium. `option.selected = true` wins whatever the tree order, and removing the `selected` attribute unselects even a dirty option. Only the scratch probes caught that. The reset also had to bind at the one child-list choke point (`_insert`/`_detach`), and that exposed a latent bug: `replaceChild` inserted before it removed, so the reset saw the wrong order. The suite moves bound on test-side assumptions, not on the select model:
- synthetic presses are not in the tree, and the router drops anything `container.contains` refuses;
- `common.js` replaces a load-time `window.api` stub;
- `proxy.js` reads its elements at load, so it needs `scripts: []` and then `run`;
- the real serializer writes `selected=""`, which made one negative regex assertion pass vacuously.

**2. What I'd do first.** I'd run the Chromium probe before writing any model code. I did that mostly, but late for the attribute cases. I'd also grep each suite's press shim for what it assumes about containment before moving it.

**3. What I'd tidy.**
- The synthetic press plus `contains = () => true` now lives in two suites (`prompt-section-task-mode`, `lin-3833`). It belongs in `client-world` as a named helper.
- The proxy-page extraction (regex over `renderProxyPage`) is duplicated in `lin-3136` and `lin-4296-scope-pick`.
- `add`/`item`/`namedItem` throw on every element, not just `<select>`.
- The reset writes selectedness without dirtiness, a documented simplification.

**4. What this ticket would have been.** If suites drove drawn buttons, or shared one press helper, and census stops were data naming symbols, it would have been "model `<select>`; three entries leave". No caret rewrite, no per-suite shims.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- The ticket conflated reset and write. The Surveys caught that, along with the mislabelled task-mode stop.
- The plan put the witness cases inside the moved suites, which contradicts "counts unchanged". I moved them to new files.
- The conditional catalog-apply test never applied, because no catalog fetch resolves in those suites.
- The plan's expectation of 1–3 moves was right. All three moved (2 for the select model, 1 for another reason).

**6. What it left behind.**
- New without an obvious home: `lin-4296-dispatch-reader` and `lin-4296-scope-pick`, ticket-named files that hold witnesses belonging to their subjects' suites.
- In two places: the press shim and the proxy markup cut.
- Things that didn't learn about it: `public/ship.js:1154` calls `select.remove(1)`, which the fake now refuses instead of silently detaching the select. Nothing tracks that callsite. LIN-4297's list may still name `browserMarkup`. The census comments still pin line numbers.
- Simpler: `browserMarkup`/`useRealDisclosure` are gone, the two reader stubs are gone, three hand-written fakes are gone (census 25 → 22), and every fake-backed suite now gets spec-ordered `replaceChild` and a real `<select>` instead of `undefined`.
